scenes.visual: Title card 'Pulses, Not Amount' over the three stacked boxes from the first film, the top box crossed out. Same COLOUR MAP as the first film: COLOUR MAP, same in both films and in the lesson: GnRH GOLD; LH BLUE; FSH GREEN; testosterone and estradiol ORANGE-RED; inhibin B PURPLE; progesterone TEAL. The hypothalamus, pituitary and gonad are always three stacked rounded boxes, top to bottom, labelled 'hypothalamus', 'pituitary', 'gonad'. Cream background, 16:9. Hormone levels are schematic bars and traces labelled 'schematic'; nothing is drawn as a molecule. A pump cartoon is grey with a GOLD output tube.

scenes.tts: Same hormone, same monkey. Could the timing of a signal matter as much as its amount? The first film showed G n R H reaching the pituitary in pulses. This film asks whether the pulse is the message.
scenes.caption: Same hormone, same monkey. Could the timing of a signal matter as much as its amount? The first film showed GnRH reaching the pituitary in pulses. This film asks whether the pulse is the message.
scenes.visual: Split screen: left, a steady GOLD stream into a pituitary box; right, separate GOLD bursts into a pituitary box; a question mark over each, no tick or cross yet. Then a quick inset of the first film's loop with GOLD pulses ticking down the portal tube.
scenes.narration: Same hormone, same monkey. Could the timing of a signal matter as much as its amount? The first film showed GnRH reaching the pituitary in pulses. This film asks whether the pulse is the message.

scenes.tts: Ernst Knobil's laboratory worked with female rhesus monkeys. Damage to the hypothalamus, called a lesion, had stopped their L H and F S H. But the pituitary itself was still intact.
scenes.caption: Ernst Knobil's laboratory worked with female rhesus monkeys. Damage to the hypothalamus, called a lesion, had stopped their LH and FSH. But the pituitary itself was still intact.
scenes.visual: A rhesus monkey cartoon; zoom to the three boxes. The top box is crossed out, label 'hypothalamic lesion', and the portal tube is broken. The pituitary box stays solid, label 'pituitary intact'. Text on screen: '1978'.
scenes.narration: Ernst Knobil's laboratory worked with female rhesus monkeys. Damage to the hypothalamus, called a lesion, had stopped their LH and FSH. But the pituitary itself was still intact.

scenes.tts: The design is simple. Remove the animal's own source of a hormone. Then give it back from outside on different schedules, with the steady one giving at least as much in total.
scenes.visual: Three-step strip, left to right: 'remove the source' (top box crossed out), 'give it back from outside' (pump), 'compare delivery patterns' (a GOLD burst train above a GOLD steady stream, with two side bars labelled 'total per day, schematic': the steady bar equal to or taller than the pulse bar, tag 'steady: at least as much').
scenes.narration: The design is simple. Remove the animal's own source of a hormone. Then give it back from outside on different schedules, with the steady one giving at least as much in total.

scenes.tts: It also needed a clean supply of the hormone. G n R H had just been isolated. Pure synthetic G n R H made this kind of experiment possible.
scenes.caption: It also needed a clean supply of the hormone. GnRH had just been isolated. Pure synthetic GnRH made this kind of experiment possible.
scenes.visual: A small vial labelled 'synthetic GnRH' with a GOLD liquid is loaded into the pump cartoon; the pump's GOLD tube connects to the pituitary box.
scenes.narration: It also needed a clean supply of the hormone. GnRH had just been isolated. Pure synthetic GnRH made this kind of experiment possible.

scenes.tts: So the team could give G n R H through a vein. They read the pituitary's answer in blood samples. With no drive from above, the L H record started flat.
scenes.caption: So the team could give GnRH through a vein. They read the pituitary's answer in blood samples. With no drive from above, the LH record started flat.
scenes.visual: A pump cartoon takes the place of the crossed-out top box, with a GOLD tube to the pituitary. Below, a time axis labelled 'days' draws; a BLUE trace labelled 'LH in blood (schematic)' runs flat along the bottom. A small inset magnifies a few hours to show the pulse spacing, label 'one pulse each hour'. To the side, an empty two-bar chart labelled 'GnRH per day (schematic)'.
scenes.narration: So the team could give GnRH through a vein. They read the pituitary's answer in blood samples. With no drive from above, the LH record started flat.

scenes.tts: First, brief infusions, once every hour. The pump gives a short burst, then stops, then bursts again. Hourly pulses restored L H and F S H secretion, and kept it going.
scenes.caption: First, brief infusions, once every hour. The pump gives a short burst, then stops, then bursts again. Hourly pulses restored LH and FSH secretion, and kept it going.
scenes.visual: The pump emits short GOLD bursts with gaps, a small clock icon ticking 'once an hour'. The BLUE trace rises off the floor and stays up with a regular rhythm (schematic). A GREEN dashed line labelled 'FSH' rises with it. The left bar of the side chart fills, label 'pulses'.
scenes.narration: First, brief infusions, once every hour. The pump gives a short burst, then stops, then bursts again. Hourly pulses restored LH and FSH secretion, and kept it going.

scenes.tts: Now switch the pump to a steady stream. Set it high enough that each day it delivers at least as much G n R H as the pulses. Will L H stay up, rise higher, or fall away?
scenes.caption: Now switch the pump to a steady stream. Set it high enough that each day it delivers at least as much GnRH as the pulses. Will LH stay up, rise higher, or fall away?
scenes.visual: The GOLD bursts merge into one unbroken GOLD stream. The right bar of the side chart fills to the same height as the left bar or taller, label 'steady: at least as much (schematic)'. The BLUE trace stops at a dashed vertical line, with three arrows beyond it: 'stay up?', 'higher?', 'fall?'.
scenes.narration: Now switch the pump to a steady stream. Set it high enough that each day it delivers at least as much GnRH as the pulses. Will LH stay up, rise higher, or fall away?

scenes.visual: Predict pause. The three arrows hold; a 5-second ring timer counts down at bottom right.

scenes.tts: It falls away. The steady supply did not sustain L H and F S H. If the pituitary counted only the total, the steady drip would have done at least as well. It did not.
scenes.caption: It falls away. The steady supply did not sustain LH and FSH. If the pituitary counted only the total, the steady drip would have done at least as well. It did not.
scenes.visual: On the days axis, beyond the dashed line, the BLUE trace and GREEN dashed line are not sustained: they decline over the following days, not an instant drop; label 'not sustained (schematic, not the paper's data)'. The two side bars stay visible: steady bar equal or taller, LH falling.
scenes.narration: It falls away. The steady supply did not sustain LH and FSH. If the pituitary counted only the total, the steady drip would have done at least as well. It did not.

scenes.tts: Then the team went back to hourly pulses. The authors reported that secretion came back. So the pituitary had not been damaged. It could still answer, when the timing was right.
scenes.visual: The GOLD stream breaks back into hourly bursts. The BLUE trace climbs again and resumes its rhythm (schematic). A tick appears on the pituitary box, label 'still able to respond'.
scenes.narration: Then the team went back to hourly pulses. The authors reported that secretion came back. So the pituitary had not been damaged. It could still answer, when the timing was right.

scenes.tts: So the pituitary reads the timing of G n R H, not only its total. Hourly pulses keep it working. A steady supply, even a larger one, did not.
scenes.caption: So the pituitary reads the timing of GnRH, not only its total. Hourly pulses keep it working. A steady supply, even a larger one, did not.
scenes.visual: The whole BLUE trace sits under a GOLD input strip: bursts, steady, bursts, with the LH response under each segment. Labels: 'pulses: LH up', 'steady: LH not sustained', 'pulses again: LH up'. No receptor or molecule is drawn; no mechanism is shown.
scenes.narration: So the pituitary reads the timing of GnRH, not only its total. Hourly pulses keep it working. A steady supply, even a larger one, did not.

scenes.tts: This experiment has limits. It shows the rule in these monkeys. It does not show where the pulses come from, or what interval between pulses is normal in people. Nor does it show why a steady supply fails.
scenes.visual: A small card with two grey question marks: 'where do pulses come from?' and 'normal interval in people?' and 'why does steady fail?'. The monkey cartoon stays in the corner, label 'rhesus monkeys'.
scenes.narration: This experiment has limits. It shows the rule in these monkeys. It does not show where the pulses come from, or what interval between pulses is normal in people. Nor does it show why a steady supply fails.

scenes.visual: End card with Hex. LINE: 'The pituitary reads the timing of GnRH, not only its total.'
